                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> And love the uppermostrooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 And greetings in the markets, and to be cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led of men Rabbi, Rabbi.<ns0:note place="bottom">We have the same applyed to the <ns0:hi>Scribes. Mark</ns0:hi> 12.38, 39. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 11.43. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> addeth, <ns0:hi>which love to go in long Clothing.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour in these Words doth not blame a Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stinction in Habits, and places; for he himself hath taught us, that those who are in Kings Palaces wear soft Rayment, and being often called <ns0:hi>Master</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Lord,</ns0:hi> never reflected on them, who called him so, as having done amiss, he only blameth the <ns0:hi>Pharisees Ambition,</ns0:hi> and silly Affectation of these little things, seeking their own Honour, and Glory, or an undue Domina<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion; there is therefore an <ns0:hi>Emphasis</ns0:hi> to be put upon the Word <ns0:hi>Love.</ns0:hi> They might take <ns0:hi>Salutations,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>upper Rooms,</ns0:hi> if offered them as their due, for keeping Civil orders, but not affect them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 But be not ye called Rabbi,<ns0:note n="*" place="margin">James 3 <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> for one is your
<ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:261" />
master <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> Christ, and all ye are brethren.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 And call no man your father upon the earth, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ma<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 1.6.</ns0:note> for one is your Father which is in hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 Neither be ye called masters, for one is your master, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> Christ.<ns0:note place="bottom">It is most certain that our Saviour doth not here forbid the giving of the Titles of <ns0:hi>Masters</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Fathers</ns0:hi> to his Ministers. for then <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> would not have given himself the Title of <ns0:hi>Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 4.15. nor called the <ns0:hi>Galathians</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>little Chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren, Gal.</ns0:hi> 4.19. nor called <ns0:hi>Timothy</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>Son,</ns0:hi> and himself his Father, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 2.22. nor call'd himself a <ns0:hi>Doctor</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 2.7.2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.11. That which he forbids, is 1. An <ns0:hi>Affectation</ns0:hi> of such <ns0:hi>Titles,</ns0:hi> and hunting after them. 2. <ns0:hi>Rem Ti<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="4 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi> the Exercise of an absolute <ns0:hi>Mastership,</ns0:hi> or a <ns0:hi>Paternal absolute Power.</ns0:hi> So as to require any to believe things because they said them, or to do things because they bid them, with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out seeing the things asserted, or first commanded in the Word of God. For in that Sense God alone is Mens Father. Christ a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lone their <ns0:hi>Masters. Pastors</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Teachers</ns0:hi> in the Church, are all but Ministers, Ministers of Christ to publish his Will; and to injoyn his Laws, nor must any be owned as <ns0:hi>Masters</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Fathers</ns0:hi> to impose their Laws, and Doctrines. This is twice repeated, because such is the Corruption of humane Nature, that it is very prone, not only to affect these swelling Titles, but also to exercise these Exorbitant Authorities.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 20.26, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> But he that is greatest amongst you shall be your servant.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Prov. 29.23. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 4.6. 1 Pet. 5.5.</ns0:note> whosoever shall exalt himself, shall be abased, and he that shall humble himself, shall be exalted.<ns0:note place="bottom">We have what is <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 12. twice in <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch,</ns0:hi> 14.11. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 18.14. These Verses expound what went before, and let us know. 1. That it was not a <ns0:hi>Title,</ns0:hi> but the <ns0:hi>Affectation</ns0:hi> of a <ns0:hi>Title</ns0:hi> which he blamed. 2. Not a <ns0:hi>Doctorship,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Master<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ship,</ns0:hi> but such a <ns0:hi>Doctorship,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Mastership,</ns0:hi> as made a man too big for the Ministry of the Church; such Honour as lifted up the Mans Heart above his Work. He is an Infamous <ns0:hi>Doctor</ns0:hi> in the Church of Christ, who thinks himself too <ns0:hi>High,</ns0:hi> or too great to be a Minister in it. For God will abase, and Men shall abase him who exalteth himself. God resisteth, and Men usu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ally contemn and despise the <ns0:hi>Proud,</ns0:hi> especially Ministers who are so. Both God shall <ns0:hi>Exalt,</ns0:hi> and Men shall Honour those that humble themselves both <ns0:hi>to Men,</ns0:hi> Condescending to those of low Degree, and to <ns0:hi>their Work</ns0:hi> thinking not the mean<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />est Ministry to Souls, a Work beneath them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 But woe unto you Scribes, and Pharisees, hy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pocrites, for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in your selves, neither will ye suffer them that are entring, to go in.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Saviour now cometh to denounce Eight Woes against the <ns0:hi>Teachers</ns0:hi> of those times, the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisies, Luke</ns0:hi> saith. <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 11.52. <ns0:hi>Woe unto you Lawyers, for you take away the Key of knowledge, you entred not in your selves, and them that were entring you hindred.</ns0:hi> It was written of old, that the Priests Lips should preserve knowledge, God hath committed the <ns0:hi>Key of Knowledge</ns0:hi> to the Ministers and Guides of his Church, not that they should take it away, but that the people might <ns0:hi>seek the Law at their Mouths, because they are the Messengers of the Lord of Hosts. Mal.</ns0:hi> 2.7. Now saith our Saviour, you have <ns0:hi>taken it away,</ns0:hi> this <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> calls a <ns0:hi>Shutting up the Kingdom of Heaven against Men.</ns0:hi> Doing what in them lay to keep Men from the Knowledge of the Mind and Will of God, neither themselves Teaching them the Knowledge of God, which yet was their Office and Duty, nor suffering others to do it who would. <ns0:hi>You will neither go in your selves, neither will you suffer them that are entring to go in.</ns0:hi> Your selves are too Proud, or Lazy to Preach the Gospel, which is the way to the Kingdom of Heaven, and when others would, you suffer them not, nor yet will you suffer the People, who have an Heart to it, to hear it. For this he calls them Hypocrites seven times in this Chapter, they pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tending to be Teachers, and openers of the Door to the Kingdom of Heaven, when indeed they did shut it, and de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ounceth a <ns0:hi>Woe</ns0:hi> to them, comprehending that ruin which soon after came upon them, and their City by the Roman Armies, and that Eternal Damnation which slept not, and was due to them. There are no worser Men in the World than <ns0:hi>Hypocries,</ns0:hi> Men pretending highly to God, yet neither themselves doing their Duty in imbracing the Gospel, nor suffering others to do it, but doing what in them lye, to hin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der People from the means, by which they might come to the Kingdom of Heaven.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 Woe unto you scribes, and Pharisees, hy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pocrites, for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Tim. 3.6. Tit. 1.11.</ns0:note> ye devour widows houses, and for a pretence make long prayers, therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 12.40. and <ns0:hi>Luke Ch.</ns0:hi> 20.47. If any should think that <ns0:hi>Long Prayers</ns0:hi> are here condemned, he will be Confuted, by <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 6.12. where he will find that our Saviour <ns0:hi>continued all Night in Prayer to God.</ns0:hi> It is the end of their long Prayers, which alone our Saviour bla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />meth, their making them a <ns0:hi>Pretence to devour Widows Hou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses.</ns0:hi> Which whether they did as interested in the <ns0:hi>Civil Power</ns0:hi> (in which it is certain the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> amongst the Jews were imployed) or by Vertue of their <ns0:hi>Ecclesiastical Power,</ns0:hi> or Influence, perswading silly Women to give them their E<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tates, or at least to give them a great part of them, to the Service of the Tabernacle, that they might pray for their Souls, was an Abomination to God, not only for the Hopocrify of such Prayers designed for another end than they pretended, but because God had taken upon him the special care<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> and pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tection of the Widows. As our Saviour had before blamed their Religious Acts for the <ns0:hi>Ostentation</ns0:hi> in them, seeking on<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly their own Honour, and Applause: So he here blameth them for their Covetous design in them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 Woe unto you scribes, and Pharisees, hy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pocrites, for ye compass sea and land, to make one proselyte: and when he is made, ye make him two fold more the children of hell than your selves.<ns0:note place="bottom">A third <ns0:hi>Woe</ns0:hi> followeth, expressed in this Verse, because they Corrupted their <ns0:hi>Proselytes,</ns0:hi> both as to Doctrine and Man<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ners, so as they were twice more the Children of the Devil, and in danger of Hell than before. A <ns0:hi>Proselyte was one,</ns0:hi> who coming from some <ns0:hi>Pagan</ns0:hi> Nation Relinquished Idols, and worshipped one true, and living God. Of these Writers tell us there were two sorts: One that only professed to <ns0:hi>believe</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Worship one God.</ns0:hi> tho he did not embrace the Jewish Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ligion, such a one they suffered to live among<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t them, and cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led him <ns0:hi>a Proselyte of the Gate.</ns0:hi> Others imbraced the Jewish Religion, and were admitted into their Church, by <ns0:hi>Circumci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Baptisme</ns0:hi> and Sacrifice (as their Writers tell us) These they called <ns0:hi>Proselytes</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Righteousness.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour saith the Scribes, and Pharisees, <ns0:hi>Compassed Sea and Land,</ns0:hi> that is, would take any pains (it is a Proverbial Expre<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sion) to make one a <ns0:hi>Prose<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>yte,</ns0:hi> nor was this blame-worthy in them, but that which followeth, <ns0:hi>That they made him twice more the Children of Hell, than before.</ns0:hi> Corrupting them with their false Doctrine, and setting them Examples of an ill Life. Their business was not to turn them from Sin unto God, but meerly to convert them to an Opinion, if they had once got them into their Church, so as they could make their Markets of them, never regarding their Souls more, nor to press upon them the Reformation of their Lives, that they might be saved. Thus <ns0:hi>Priests</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iesuites</ns0:hi> at this Day go to <ns0:hi>China, Iapan,</ns0:hi> to Proselyte Men to the Roman Faith, and use all imaginable Arts to seduce Persons Born and bred under the Profe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sion of the Protestant Religion, in Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />testant Countries, and boast much of their Converts, but he who looks upon the Scriptures, and considereth the Lives of the most of their Converts, will easily see they are but twice more the Children of Hell, being Licensed, by their Indulgences, pardons, Absolutions, nay by their very Casuilts to live most Prodigious Impious Lives, to say nothing of their Damnable Errors in matters of Faith.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 Woe unto you <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 15 14.</ns0:note> ye blind guides, which say, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ch. 5.33, 34.</ns0:note> Whosoever shall swear by the temple it is no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing, but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 You fools, and blind, for whether <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> great<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er, the gold or the temple, which sanctifieth the gold?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing, but whosoever sweareth by the gift that is upon it, he is guilty. <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>a debtor or bound.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 Ye fools, and blind: for whether is greater the gift, or <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 29 37</ns0:note> the altar that sanctifyeth the gift?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 Whosoever therefore shall swear by the al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tar, sweareth by it, and by all things there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 And whoso shall swear by the temple, sweareth by it, and by <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Kin. 8.13. 2 Chro. 6.2.</ns0:note> him that dwelleth there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />in.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 And he that shall swear by heaven, swear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth by the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 5.34. Acts 7.49.</ns0:note> throne of God, and by him that sit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teth thereon.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Saviour here sheweth the false Doctrine, which the <ns0:hi>Pha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />risees</ns0:hi> for their own Gain taught the People, concerning <ns0:hi>Oaths.</ns0:hi> God had Commanded that they should fear and serve the Lord their God, and <ns0:hi>swear by his Name. Deut.</ns0:hi> 6.13. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 10.20. He that <ns0:hi>sweareth</ns0:hi> by any Person, or thing, doth two things. He attributeth to the thing, or Person, by which he sweareth a knowledge of the Heart, and the secret intention. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> He calleth upon the Person or thing<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> by which he sweareth to be his Judge; or to take a revenge upon him, in Case, he doth not believe in his Heart, what he affirmeth, or denieth with his Words, to be true or false, otherwise an Oath is no security at all. From whence appeareth, that it is unreasonable for any to swear by any other than God, who alone can have a know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledge of the Truth, and security of the Heart; and that he, who sweareth by any Creature, committeth Idolatry in his Heart, and in his Heart doth indeed Blaspheme, paying a Divine Ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mage to a Creature, and attributing to the Creature, what only agreeth to the Creature. The <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> as it seemeth had taught the People, that it was Lawful to swear by the Crea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture; but all <ns0:hi>Oaths</ns0:hi> by Creatures did not bind to the perfor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mance of the thing promised by such Oaths: If a Man swear by the <ns0:hi>Temple,</ns0:hi> or by the <ns0:hi>Altar, It was nothing,</ns0:hi> no Man was bound by such Oaths, to perform the thing, for which such <ns0:hi>Oaths</ns0:hi> was given as a security. But if any Man swear by the <ns0:hi>Gold of the Temple,</ns0:hi> or by <ns0:hi>a Gift,</ns0:hi> which he brought to the <ns0:hi>Altar,</ns0:hi> these <ns0:hi>Oaths</ns0:hi> did bind him. By the <ns0:hi>Gold of the Temple,</ns0:hi> is not to be understood the <ns0:hi>Golden Vessels</ns0:hi> used in the Temple; nor the <ns0:hi>Golden Plates,</ns0:hi> with which the several parts of the Temple shined; but the <ns0:hi>Gold</ns0:hi> which was brought as an <ns0:hi>Offer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing</ns0:hi> into the <ns0:hi>Temple,</ns0:hi> and put into the Treasury there, of which and of the Gifts the Priests and Officers about the Temple, had a considerable share, which made them Equalize an Oath by these, to an Oath made by the Name of God it self: Our Saviour here sheweth the unreasonable Folly o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> the Tradition, and calleth them for it, <ns0:hi>Blind Guides,</ns0:hi> for in reason: The <ns0:hi>Temple</ns0:hi> Sanctifying the Gold<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> must it self be more especially Holy, that is, separate for an Holy use. The <ns0:hi>Temple</ns0:hi> was Holy, so was the <ns0:hi>Altar</ns0:hi> before the <ns0:hi>Gold</ns0:hi> was brought into it, but the <ns0:hi>Gold</ns0:hi> was not Holy, till it was brought into the Holy place, and there offered. 2. Secondly, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e lets them know, that Oaths by the Creatures once made did oblige, as much as if they had been made by God himself. They were indeed sinfully made, for Men ought not to have sworn by Creatures, but being made, those who made them were bound to perform them, if the matter of them were not sinful. For he that swears by the <ns0:hi>Altar,</ns0:hi> swears by it, and all the things thereon: And he who swears by the <ns0:hi>Temple,</ns0:hi> swears by it, and him that dwelleth therein: And he who swears by Heaven, swears <ns0:hi>by the Throne of God, and him that sitteth thereon.</ns0:hi> For none who sware by inanimate things, could possibly be imagined to call these things which he knew had no Life, no Sense, no knowledge to be a Witness to the Truth of his Heart, as to what he <ns0:hi>be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieved,</ns0:hi> or what he <ns0:hi>intended.</ns0:hi> So as though he that sweareth by the Creature, be a <ns0:hi>profane Swearer,</ns0:hi> yet he is <ns0:hi>bound by his Oath,</ns0:hi> he indeed swearing <ns0:hi>by the God of those Creatures.</ns0:hi> He hath reason to repent or the profane, and unlawful form of his Oath; but if the matter be, what he may without sin per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />form, he is bound by his Oath to the performance of it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:262" />23 Woe unto you scribes and pharisees, hypo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crites, for ye pay tithe of mint, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Gr. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. Dill.</ns0:note> and Annise and Cummin, and have <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Sam. 15.22. Hos. 6.6. Mic. 6.8. Chap. 9.13. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 12.7.</ns0:note> omitted the weightier mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.<ns0:note place="bottom">We have much the same, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 11.42. only there it is, <ns0:hi>Ye Tithe Mint, and Rue,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>all manner of Herbs, and pass over Iudgment, and the Love of God.</ns0:hi> It is manifest by our Saviours words in the latter part of the Verse: <ns0:hi>These ought you to have done</ns0:hi>; that he doth not blame the <ns0:hi>Pharisees exactness</ns0:hi> in Tithing <ns0:hi>Mint, Annise, Rue, Cummin,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>all manner of Herbs.</ns0:hi> But their neglecting the <ns0:hi>Weightier matters of the Law<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Faith</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Love to God, Iudgment</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mercy.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Levites</ns0:hi> having no Inheritance, God ordained <ns0:hi>Tithes</ns0:hi> for their Maintenance; of which also the poor were to have a share, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 27.30. <ns0:hi>Num.</ns0:hi> 18.23. The <ns0:hi>Pharisee</ns0:hi> boa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ted, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 18.12. That he paid Tithe of all he possest; Christ here ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />knowledgeth, that the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> were exact in their paying <ns0:hi>Tithes.</ns0:hi> But he blames them for their Partiality, neglecting the weightier things of the Law. 2. For their <ns0:hi>Hypocrisie,</ns0:hi> they were only exact in these little things, that they might be taken notice of, as <ns0:hi>Scrupulous</ns0:hi> observers of the <ns0:hi>Divine Law</ns0:hi>; while they omitted those things, which were of much more weight, which he reckoneth up: <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> by which some understand Faith in God, but the most, <ns0:hi>Faithfulness,</ns0:hi> and sincere and ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nest dealings with Men, in opposition to Fraud, and Cheat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, and Circumventions, <ns0:hi>Iudgment,</ns0:hi> by which he means <ns0:hi>Iustice,</ns0:hi> giving to every one what is their own: <ns0:hi>Mercy,</ns0:hi> by which he meaneth a Charitable behaviour, in helping such as are miserable, and afflicted. <ns0:hi>Love to God,</ns0:hi> which is the true Root, out of which all things should flow, and is indeed com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />prehensive of all our Duty toward God, as well as the <ns0:hi>Root</ns0:hi> of all our <ns0:hi>Good Works</ns0:hi> towards Men.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 Ye blind guides, which strain at a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>gnat, and swallow a camel.<ns0:note place="bottom">It is a <ns0:hi>Proverbial Expression</ns0:hi> used amongst them, against such as would pretend a great Niceness and Scrupulosity, about, and Zeal for, little things, but in matters of much higher Concern, and moment were not Nice, and Scrupulous at all, and this indeed is both a certain Note, and an ordinary Pra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctice of Hypocrites: There is no man that is sincere in his Obedience to God, but hath respect to all Gods Commande<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 119. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 6. Tho some Duties be greater, of more moment for the Honour and Glory of God than others, which a good Man will lay the greatest stress upon, yet he will neglect nothing which the Law of God enjoyneth him: But concerning Hypocrites, these two things are always true. 1. They are partial in their pretended Obedience. 2. They always lay the greatest stress upon the least things of the Law, bodily Labour, and Exercise, and those things which require least of the Heart, and least self-denial.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 Woe unto you Scribes and Pharisees, hy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pocrites: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mar. 7.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> for ye make clean the out-side of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that <ns0:hi>which is</ns0:hi> within the cup and platter, that the out<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />side of them may be clean also.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath this, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 11.39, 40. as occasioned by the <ns0:hi>Pha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />risees,</ns0:hi> wondring that he washed not before Dinner, instead of <ns0:hi>Extortion</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Excess,</ns0:hi> he hath <ns0:hi>ravening</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Wickedness,</ns0:hi> and addeth, <ns0:hi>You Fools, did not he that made that which is with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out, make that which is within also?</ns0:hi> But the same thing might be spoken at two speveral times: He speaketh there to the <ns0:hi>Pharisee,</ns0:hi> with whom he Dined, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 37. Here he speaks to the <ns0:hi>Disciples,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Multitude.</ns0:hi> Our Saviours design here seemeth to me not to be a Condemning of their <ns0:hi>Legal,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Traditional washings of Pots</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Cups,</ns0:hi> which he elsewhere reflecteth up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on, but by way of allusion only; to blame them that in their whole Conversation, they rather studied an external Purity, than the inward Purity of the Heart, whereas if they would first have looked at Purity of Heart, the other would have followed that. A man may be outwardly pure, and inwardly filthy and impure: But no man can have a pure Heart, but he will live a Pure and Holy Life; for the <ns0:hi>External Acts,</ns0:hi> are but the Imperate Acts of the Soul: <ns0:hi>Out of the abundance of the Heart, the Mouth speaketh,</ns0:hi> and according to the In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clinations, and Affections of the Heart the Foot moveth, the Hand, and all the bodily Members act. For our Saviours Ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plication of this to their <ns0:hi>Traditional washings,</ns0:hi> I shall speak to it when I come to, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 11.39.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 Woe unto you Scribes and Pharisees, hy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pocrites, for ye are like unto whited sepulchers, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead mens bones, and of all un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cleanness.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 Even so ye also appear outwardly righte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous unto men, unto men, but within ye are full of hypo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crisie, and iniquity.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Similitude is of the same import, with the other to shew, that the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> had only a Vizour of strictness, and Holiness, when in the mean time their Hearts were full of <ns0:hi>Lusts, Hypocrisie</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iniquity.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had two sorts of <ns0:hi>Graves</ns0:hi>; some for ordinary Persons which appeared not (to which our Saviour likened the <ns0:hi>Pharisees, Luk.</ns0:hi> 11.44.) Others that were covered with <ns0:hi>Tombes,</ns0:hi> which were wont to be kept whited, so as they looked very fair outwardly, but had within nothing but Rottenness and Putrefaction. To these he com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pareth them in this place. They were Men that made a great shew, but had nothing of any inward Purity or cleanness, but were full of Iniquity: Thus <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> called <ns0:hi>Ananias</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>w<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ted Wall,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 5.9. The <ns0:hi>Psalmist</ns0:hi> saith of the Throat of the Wicked, that it is an <ns0:hi>open Sepulcher.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 11.47.</ns0:note> Woe unto you Scribes and Pharisees, hy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pocrites, because ye build the tombs of the pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets, and garnish the sepulchers of the righteous.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 And say, if we had been in the days our Fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath it, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 11.44. <ns0:hi>Woe unto you, for you Build the Sepulchers of the Prophets, and your Fathers killed them: Truly you bear Witness, that you allow the Deeds of your Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers, for they indeed killed them, and you build their Sepulchers.</ns0:hi> It is plain by our Saviours discourse, that the <ns0:hi>Pha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />risees</ns0:hi> were at great Charge oft times, to rebuild or adorn the Sepulchers of the Lords <ns0:hi>Prophets,</ns0:hi> who had been slain by the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> in former Ages, for testifying the Truth of God, and the <ns0:hi>Sepulchers</ns0:hi> of other <ns0:hi>Righteous Men</ns0:hi> dying for their <ns0:hi>Righte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ousness.</ns0:hi> This they did like a Company of <ns0:hi>Hypocrites,</ns0:hi> to per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swade the World of what they also said. That <ns0:hi>had they lived in the times of those Prophets,</ns0:hi> and other good Men, <ns0:hi>they would have had no Hand in their Blood.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 Wherefore ye be witnesses unto your selves, that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Act. 7.51, 52. 1 Thes. 2.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> ye are the children of them that killed the prophets.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 Fill ye up then the measure of your Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:262" />33 Ye serpents, <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ap 3.7.</ns0:note> ye generation of Vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?<ns0:note place="bottom">You (saith our <ns0:hi>Lord</ns0:hi>) confess that you are lineally descended from those who killed the Prophets: You have not only their Blood communicated to you, but their Spirit, your Behaviours and Carriages towards me, and my Disciples have witnessed, and will yet further testifie, that you are the Children of those who killed the Prophets in a Moral, as well as a natural Sense; you inherit the same Spirit, and are full of the same Malice and Rancor. They killed them, and you bury them: Seeing there is no reclaiming you, Go you on, <ns0:hi>Fill up the mea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sure of your Fathers sins.</ns0:hi> There is something more to be added, to make the Iniquity of this Nation full; you are a Company of <ns0:hi>Serpents, Vipers,</ns0:hi> that cannot escape the <ns0:hi>Dam<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nation of Hell.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 Wherefore behold, I send unto you Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets, and wise men, and scribes, and <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ct. 5.40.22.19.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>some</ns0:hi> of them ye shall kill and crucifie, and <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>hap. 10.17. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Cor. 11.24, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>some</ns0:hi> of them ye shall scourge in your Synagogues, and perse<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cute <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> from city to city.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>en. 48.</ns0:note> from the blood of righteous Abel, unto the blood of Zacharias, the son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 11.49.50. <ns0:hi>Therefore also said the Wis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom of God, I will send them Prophets and Apostles, and some of them they shall slay, and persecute. That the Blood of all the Prophets, which was shed from the Foundation, of the World, may be required of this Generation. From the Blood of Abel, to the Blood of Zacharias, who pe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rished between the Altar and the Temple. Verily I say un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to you, it shall be required of this Generation. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Therefore also said the Wisdom of God. Matthew</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Behold I send.</ns0:hi> Christ is the Wisdom of God, he here tells them, he would send them <ns0:hi>Prophets, Wise men, Scribes. Luke</ns0:hi> expounds it by <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Apostles.</ns0:hi> Men Authorized by Christ, to reveal unto Men the Will of God, and Men that should be extraordinarily inspired to inable them thereunto. <ns0:hi>Scribes,</ns0:hi> that is Persons instructed to the Kingdom of God, a new sort of <ns0:hi>Scribes,</ns0:hi> but much sitter for their Work, than the present <ns0:hi>Scribes. And some you shall kill, and crucifie, &c.</ns0:hi> Our Lord in this only fore-tells, what usage both himself and his Apostles should meet with from them, which was fulfilled, in what the Scripture telleth us, of the scourging of <ns0:hi>Paul,</ns0:hi> the stoning of <ns0:hi>Stephen,</ns0:hi> the killing of <ns0:hi>Iames,</ns0:hi> &c. beside the Crucifying of himself. <ns0:hi>That upon</ns0:hi> you; that is, as he expounds it, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 38. <ns0:hi>Vpon this Generation may come all the Righteous Blood, that is, the Blood of righteous men, from the Blood of Abel,</ns0:hi> to the Blood of <ns0:hi>Zachariah, shed upon the Earth,</ns0:hi> &c. Here arise two Questions. 1. Who this <ns0:hi>Zacha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />riah</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Barachiah</ns0:hi> was? 2. <ns0:hi>How it could stand with Gods justice, to bring the Guilt of the Blood of former Genera<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions, upon that Generation.</ns0:hi> As to the first, some have guest the Person spoken of, to have been one <ns0:hi>Zachariah</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Ba<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ruch,</ns0:hi> who was the last slain upon the taking of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Iosephus</ns0:hi> tells us, but our Saviour here speaks of a thing past, not to be afterwards done: Others think, it was <ns0:hi>Zachariah</ns0:hi> the Father of <ns0:hi>Iohn Baptist,</ns0:hi> but we have no Proo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> that he dyed a violent Death: Others think, it was <ns0:hi>Zachariah,</ns0:hi> who was one of the small Prophets, but there was no <ns0:hi>Temple in his time.</ns0:hi> It is most probably concluded to be <ns0:hi>Zachariah,</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Iehojada,</ns0:hi> whom the <ns0:hi>Iews stoned with Stones,</ns0:hi> at the <ns0:hi>Commandement of Ioash: In the Court of the House of the Lord,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 24.21. The Fathers name indeed doth not agree, but first, <ns0:hi>Iehojada</ns0:hi> (as many of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had) might have two Names, some think it was this same <ns0:hi>Zechariah,</ns0:hi> who is called the Son of <ns0:hi>Ie Berechiah, Isa.</ns0:hi> 8.2. Our Saviour nameth <ns0:hi>Abel,</ns0:hi> who lived before the Law, and <ns0:hi>Zachariah,</ns0:hi> who lived <ns0:hi>under the Law,</ns0:hi> both slain for Righteousness sake; that under them he might comprehend all the Martyrs slain in those two Periods, others Judge, that these two are named, because we read of <ns0:hi>Abels</ns0:hi> Blood crying, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 4.10. and <ns0:hi>Ze<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chariah's</ns0:hi> praying (when he dyed) <ns0:hi>That the Lord would re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quire his Blood.</ns0:hi> For the other Question. It is but Righ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teous with God, to punish the sins of Parents upon their Children; and tho such Vengeance doth not ordinarily reach further than the <ns0:hi>Third and Fourth Generation,</ns0:hi> yet where succeeding Generations, go on in the same sinful Courses, it may reach further, and oft does, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 65.6. <ns0:hi>I will</ns0:hi> (saith God) <ns0:hi>Recompence into their Bosom your iniquities, and the iniquities of your Fathers together.</ns0:hi> That was the Case here. They filled up the measure of their Fathers sins. Therefore Christ tells them, that Vengeance should sleep no longer, but come upon that <ns0:hi>Generation,</ns0:hi> which hapened in the utter Destruction of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> within less than forty years after. Our Lord concludes with a <ns0:hi>Pathetical</ns0:hi> Lamen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tation over <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> and a further Confirmation of what he had said about their Ruin.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 O Jerusalem, Jerusalem! thou that killest the Prophets, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Chr. 24.21.</ns0:note> and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren together, even as an <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 17.8. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 91.4..</ns0:note> hen gathereth her chic<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />kens under <ns0:hi>her</ns0:hi> wings, and ye would not?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 Behold your house is left unto you desolate.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 118 26. Chap. 21.9.</ns0:note> Blessed <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> he that cometh in the name of the Lord.<ns0:note place="bottom">We have the same, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 13.33, 34. <ns0:hi>O Ierusalem! Ieru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />salem!</ns0:hi> The doubling of the word, sheweth the vehemency of our Saviours Affection. <ns0:hi>Thou killest the Prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee.</ns0:hi> That hast killed, and abused, and art yet going on to do the like not taking notice of the Vengeance of God upon thee before for this very sin, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 36.16, 17. <ns0:hi>Neh.</ns0:hi> 9.26. <ns0:hi>How often would I have gathered thee</ns0:hi>? Giving thee all External means, pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />per to have reformed thee, and reconcile thee to God, <ns0:hi>as an Hen gathereth her Chickens under her Wings:</ns0:hi> Which if thou hadst accepted, and imbraced, the Chickens are not safer under the Wings of the Hen, from the danger of a <ns0:hi>Kite,</ns0:hi> than thou wouldst have been from Enemies. <ns0:hi>But thou wouldst not.</ns0:hi> In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stead of hearkening to my Prophets, thou killedst them, and didst stone those sent unto thee, and so didst voluntarily re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ject me, and all my offers, and tenders of Grace, Mercy, and Protection, through the meet obstinacy of thy perverse<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Will. <ns0:hi>Behold your House is left unto you desolate.</ns0:hi> Both the Temple, in which you place such a Confidence, and your own dwelling Houses shall be destroyed, burnt and razed down, or at least left without you as Inhabitants. <ns0:hi>For I say unto you, you shall not see me henceforth, till you shall say, Blessed is he that comes in the Name of the Lord.</ns0:hi> I will appear no more to you as a publick <ns0:hi>Preacher,</ns0:hi> after two or three days for ever; and you, that the other day so envied the Peoples Acclamations to me, <ns0:hi>Blessed is he that cometh in the Name of the Lord.</ns0:hi> Shall be glad your selves, to see <ns0:hi>one of the days of the Son of Man,</ns0:hi> and shall say the same thing, <ns0:hi>Blessed is he,</ns0:hi> &c. for whereas some interpret the term <ns0:hi>Till,</ns0:hi> &c. of the day of Judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, or the time when the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> shall be converted, I take them to be strained Interpretations. <ns0:hi>Till</ns0:hi> here certainly is to be interpreted, as <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 110.1. and <ns0:hi>Math.</ns0:hi> 1.25. and this Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />porteth with the History, for after this time, our Saviour ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />peared in the <ns0:hi>Temple</ns0:hi> publickly no more. For the Disputes raised from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 7. About Gods <ns0:hi>secret Will,</ns0:hi> whether he seri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ously willed the Salvation of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> &c. I take the <ns0:hi>Affir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mative part,</ns0:hi> to have no Foundation in this Text, for <ns0:hi>would I,</ns0:hi> is plainly enough here interpreted by the foregoing Word, <ns0:hi>Sending</ns0:hi> them <ns0:hi>Prophets,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>other Ministers,</ns0:hi> to perswade them to Repentance, and <ns0:hi>Reconciliation</ns0:hi> with God. As the use of means proper to an end appear to us, Indications of the Will of him that useth them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
